name: Malagasy Romazava
description: Romazava, a leafy green and meat broth, is widely considered Madagascar's national dish - real romazava uses several specific local greens together, which aren't distinct items here, so this leans on spinach and kale for a similar leafy character.
steps_detailed: Simmer the beef with the onion and ginger in 2 cups water 30-35 minutes until tender.
Add the spinach and kale, and simmer 8-10 minutes until wilted.

name: Malagasy Vary Amin'anana
description: Vary amin'anana, rice cooked together with greens and meat into a thick, porridge-like dish, is a genuine Malagasy comfort food, real greens simmered directly into the rice rather than served alongside.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 6-7 minutes.
Add the rice and 2.5 cups water, and simmer 18-20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the spinach in the last 5 minutes until wilted and the rice is thick and porridge-like.

name: Malagasy Ravitoto
description: Ravitoto, pounded cassava leaves stewed with pork, is one of Madagascar's most beloved dishes - real cassava leaves aren't a distinct item here, so spinach stands in for a milder, less fibrous approximation.

name: Malagasy Akoho sy Voanio (Chicken with Coconut)
description: Akoho sy voanio, chicken simmered in real coconut milk, reflects Madagascar's genuine Southeast Asian ancestral and culinary ties alongside its African influences.
steps_detailed: Brown the chicken with the onion and garlic, 8-9 minutes.
Add the coconut milk and simmer 20-22 minutes until the chicken is tender.

name: Malagasy Vary sy Laoka (Rice with Side Dish)
description: Vary sy laoka, rice paired with any accompanying dish, reflects the true structure of Malagasy eating - rice is eaten at nearly every meal, with the laoka (side) considered secondary.
steps_detailed: Cook the rice separately.
Simmer the chicken with the tomatoes and a splash of water 20-22 minutes until tender.
Serve the chicken over the rice, real Malagasy meals treating the rice itself as the main component.

name: Malagasy Ranovola (Burnt Rice Water)
description: Ranovola (or ranon'ampango), water infused with the toasted rice stuck to the bottom of the pot, is a genuine Malagasy daily drink, traditionally served with every meal instead of plain water.
steps_detailed: Toast the dry rice in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring, until deeply browned and fragrant, 4-5 minutes.
Pour hot water over the toasted rice and let steep 5 minutes before straining and drinking.
